points.quote: The University defines the unacceptable use of Generative Artificial Intelligence as the act of presenting content generated by artificial intelligence tools (such as text, media, tables etc – list not exhaustive), as one’s own without proper acknowledgement, except where the nature of the assessment makes this permissible and is explicitly stated in the assessment brief.
points.anchor: Unacceptable use of Generative Artificial Intelligence
points.gist: Presenting AI-generated content as your own without acknowledgement is unacceptable, unless the assessment brief explicitly makes it permissible.

points.quote: The University will typically consider this academic misconduct as a type of plagiarism.
points.anchor: Unacceptable use of Generative Artificial Intelligence
points.gist: Unacceptable generative AI use is typically treated as academic misconduct, a type of plagiarism.

points.quote: The University will not accept a lack of understanding of the requirements for acknowledging the work of others and/or content generated by artificial intelligence tools as a legitimate defence for academic misconduct.
points.anchor: Plagiarism (including copying, self-plagiarism, collusion and use of generative artificial intelligence)
points.gist: Not understanding the acknowledgement requirements for others' work or AI content is not accepted as a defence.

points.quote: Contributions by artificial intelligence (AI) tools must also be properly acknowledged.
points.gist: Contributions by AI tools must be properly acknowledged.

points.quote: The University defines plagiarism as the act of presenting the work of another person (or people) and/or content generated by artificial intelligence (AI) tools, as one’s own without proper acknowledgement.
points.anchor: Plagiarism (including copying, self-plagiarism, collusion and use of generative artificial intelligence)
points.gist: Plagiarism is defined to include presenting AI-generated content as your own without proper acknowledgement.

points.quote: The Academic Induction Period (AIP) covers first and concurrent occurrences of plagiarism, copying, self-plagiarism, collusion and unacceptable use of generative artificial intelligence.
points.anchor: Section 3 What is the Academic Induction Period (AIP)?
points.gist: The Academic Induction Period covers first and concurrent occurrences, including unacceptable use of generative AI.

points.quote: All second and subsequent occurrences of plagiarism, copying, selfplagiarism, collusion and unacceptable use of generative artificial intelligence during the Academic Induction Period (AIP) should be considered under the Formal Procedures for Dealing with Academic Misconduct outlined in paragraphs 27 onwards.
points.anchor: Section 3 What is the Academic Induction Period (AIP)?
points.gist: Second and later occurrences during the induction period go to the formal academic misconduct procedures.

points.quote: Concurrent offences occur when a student has two or more instances of the same form of academic misconduct (either plagiarism, or copying, or selfplagiarism, or collusion or unacceptable use of Generative Artificial Intelligence) within the same assessment period, provided that it is the student’s first instances of that specific type of academic misconduct.
points.gist: Two or more instances of the same misconduct type within one assessment period, if first instances, count as concurrent offences.

points.quote: Concurrent offences of academic misconduct will not be considered repeat offences.
points.gist: Concurrent offences are not treated as repeat offences.

points.quote: Therefore, it operates an ‘Academic Induction Period (AIP)’ during which the focus of the University’s response to signs of plagiarism and/or collusion is to educate students in regard to appropriate academic practice and academic integrity rather than to penalise unacceptable academic practice.
points.anchor: Section 3 What is the Academic Induction Period (AIP)?
points.gist: During the induction period the response to plagiarism or collusion aims to educate rather than penalise.

points.quote: the first academic year of a student’s registration with the University on an undergraduate course at Level 3 or 4 only
points.anchor: Section 3 What is the Academic Induction Period (AIP)?
points.gist: The induction period includes the first year of registration on an undergraduate course at Level 3 or 4 only.

points.quote: the first teaching block on a postgraduate course
points.anchor: Section 3 What is the Academic Induction Period (AIP)?
points.gist: The induction period includes the first teaching block on a postgraduate course.

points.anchor: Section 3 What is the Academic Induction Period (AIP)?
points.gist: The induction period does not apply to direct entrants at Levels 5 and 6.
